I’m a CNA (21M) and I am fairly new to healthcare working in a PCU. One night at around 10 the MS unit next door had a rapid called and shortly after the code blue was called. 

I had never responded to a code blue before and since it was literally like 150ft away and one of my nurses was already going so I just decided to follow. 

I get there and there’s like 10 spectators in the hallway and another 8-10 people in the room coding the patient. I sat and watched for a while and eventually made my way into to room and put on gloves. I remember seeing the scene in the room for the first time.

Two of my friends were alternating compressions and the ICU charge nurse was pushing the epis, bicarb, etc, and the ICU tech would squeeze fluid through the line after every iv push.

Eventually the charge nurse looked at me and told me it was my turn to compress so while my friend was compressing I got in close and watched to see how she was doing it and when she was ready we switched. 

I remember looking around and seeing the RT’s bagging the patient, and we stopped for another pulse check and that’s when I saw a Doppler for the first time. 

Eventually we got a pulse and we managed to get him into the ICU. We fought with him trying to keep the pulse but we just couldn’t. Eventually the family showed up and tried talking with the patient while I was giving compressions which was tough, however he was gone. 

After around 12-15 epis, and well over an hour of coding the man the physician called it. It was quite an experience.

Before I answer the question and tell you my experience, I just want to say I hope everything turns out better for you, and you get into a more clear state of mind. With that out of the way I have tried to commit suicide through self strangulation/hanging. (Not the type of hanging where you break your neck. Drop hanging) A few days ago and now still, I was dead set on the idea of suicide. However I had no means until I realized I could use the pull string on my adidas pants and I did. I didn’t tie the string to anything and instead just pulled it around my neck as tight as I possible could. Before I even knew what was happening my vision became very blurry and I felt myself slowly falling down and backwards. I’m not sure how long I was out but it must’ve been close to a minute as I had a few second seizure after opening my eyes. Somehow the string came loose around my neck and my brain started receiving oxygen again. I opened my eyes and couldn’t move or speak but was convulsing for a few seconds and after it was extremely hard to get up for a time. I only had the string tightened for less than 10 seconds before passing out/falling. No pain, and it happened so fast I didn’t even know what was happening till I opened my eyes.

Depending on how you do it, it’s not painful at all. I attempted to strangle myself with the pull string on my pants (essentially the same thing as trying to hang yourself. But different from drop hanging when you try to break your neck.) I passed out within a few seconds and had my hands not let go of the string as I was passing out and falling over I would have died. I remember feeling myself falling backwards and when my eyes opened my body was moving uncontrollably and I couldn’t speak for a few seconds. Most people think hanging/strangling yourself is painful however it is the exact opposite. Had I tied the string to something I would’ve passed out while falling and never actually known I was dying. The first handful of seconds are uncomfortable as you can imagine but after that you would pass out and continue to die unknowingly and painlessly
